title: California security deposit bad-faith retention and nonrefundable clause prohibition
requirement: A landlord or successor may not claim or retain a security deposit in bad faith, or demand replacement security in bad faith, and a lease may not characterize any security as "nonrefundable."
coverage_conditions: No coverage limits stated in this part; it governs a landlord's or successor's handling of security under any lease or rental agreement.
penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
quoted_span: The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
